_what: Every episode of experiments/scenarios.yaml, scored with guardrail.kpi.compute - the same function the delivered flights use.
_not_kpi_grade: headless-kinematic topology, measured sim_speedup >> 1: functional evidence, never a contractual KPI number

_scope.kpi_bearing_this_run_why: headless-kinematic topology, measured sim_speedup >> 1: no episode can be KPI-grade (guardrail.manifest.is_kpi_grade)

_distinct_kpi_signatures.note: episodes whose KPI tables differ (status, escapes, repairs, breaches, fail-safe, outcome, goal, time to safe, true-state distance and ticks, speed, range, offset). An upper bound on behavioural variety: float jitter in repair counts splits symmetric copies

_seeds.note: a deterministic episode repeated on another seed is identical by construction, not spread

_failsafe_labels.observed_as: the escalation FSM entering RTL or Land (Shield.filter's FSM; a Brake or a Loiter is not a fail-safe trigger)

_arms.note: plumbing check only: every headless pilot ignores text, so the arms are the same flight by construction and any difference would be a harness defect. A robustness number needs a pilot that reads language.

_true_state.basis: true position, harness oracle Shield; the grant's KPI is the Shield's own count (p0_escape_rate), reported unchanged. The autopilot_* figures are the modelled LOITER / RTL / LAND's, outside the Shield's escape rate by definition

results.why: Starts below the floor. Recovery must climb, not freeze. Was a KNOWN FAILURE from 2026-10-07 to 2026-10-09: a FALSE fail-safe through edge X6. The recovery climbs from 3 m and converges (AltitudeFix sizes the climb to reach the band in one lookahead, so it slows near the floor), but the position had then been illegal for T = 5 s with the Shield still intervening, and X6, which tested duration only, sent the aircraft to RTL at 9.45 m, 0.55 m short of the floor. The grant's fail-safe is for a repair that is unsafe ("trigger fail-safe (RTL / Land) when repair is unsafe", Safety Shield p1), and this one was working. Since 2026-10-09 X6 leaves a recovery alone while its illegal depth is shown to fall (guardrail/fsm.py, x6_min_escape_mps): the flight takes G1 then G7, reaches the band at 6.3 s and completes. Re-measured 2026-10-11 on both theta readings and with the onset limit at 1 s and 0 s; the marker was removed then. With the FSM off the flight is the LEGACY one (tests/test_sweep.py). At the grant's 5 s forecast (2026-10-12) it reaches the band at 10.3 s (G1 at 0 s, G7 at 12.3 s): AltitudeFix sizes the climb to arrive in one LOOKAHEAD, so a longer lookahead climbs more gently (see altitude-recovery-depth for the arithmetic). Still one recovery, no fail-safe, and the purpose holds. Since 2026-10-29 the recovery climbs at the policy's 2 m/s cap (the Shield's recovery_law "cap", WP3-17): 7 m to the floor in 3.6 s, 36 repairs (103 before).
Commanded to climb through the ceiling for the whole flight.

altitude-floor-recovery from seven more depths: 0.5-9.5 m against the 10 m floor and 20.5-30 m against the 20 m ceiling. One recovery each, never censored, and no slower than the Shield's own recovery law allows. AltitudeFix aims 1 m inside the band (the re-entry margin) and sizes the climb to get there in one lookahead L, capped at the policy's 2 m/s: from D metres short of that aim it climbs at the cap until D = 2 L, then follows D(t) = D1 exp(-t / L) and crosses the band edge when D = 1 m. Time to safe = max(0, D0 - 2 L) / 2 + L ln(min(D0, 2 L)). At the grant's L = 5 s (2026-10-12) that is 12.0 s from the deepest cell (30 m, D0 = 11 m) and measured 11.9 s; the gate is 12.1 s, one tick above. THE GATE IS IMPLEMENTATION-DERIVED: it certifies that the recovery follows AltitudeFix's own law, not that it meets a requirement. The grant sets no target for mean time to safe (Safety Shield, KPI table: "tracked"); its one figure, `mean_time_to_safe_s: "<=2.0"` in Stress Testing's example ScenarioSpec, belongs to a dynamic-NFZ sweep, and against it these recoveries (10.9-11.9 s at 5 s, 6.8-7.8 s at 3 s) would all fail. Until 2026-10-12 the harness flew L = 3 s and the gate read "the depth at the cap plus one 3 s lookahead (8 s at the deepest)", which held with 0.2 s to spare (7.6, 6.8, 7.8 s); at 5 s those three cells take 11.7, 10.9 and 11.9 s and failed it. The finding: at the grant's forecast a recovery from below the floor is about 1.5 times slower, because the climb is sized to the lookahead, not to the cap. 3 m is not swept: that is altitude-floor-recovery's own flight, and the sweep refuses to count one flight as two scenarios. 0.5, 2 and 30 m were known failures from 2026-10-07 to 2026-10-09 (X6 sent a converging recovery to RTL after 5 s illegal; see altitude-floor-recovery). Since X6's progress test (2026-10-09) they take G1 then G7 and recover in 7.6, 6.8 and 7.8 s; re-measured 2026-10-11 on both theta readings and both onset limits, and their markers were removed then. THE LAW SINCE 2026-10-29 (WP3-17, the Shield's recovery_law "cap"): the recovery climbs or descends at the 2 m/s cap, held only so its lookahead endpoint stays a margin short of the far edge, and never slower than the old law; the one-lookahead tail is gone. Time to safe = D / 2 for D metres outside the band, plus a tick: 4.8, 4.1, 2.1 and 0.3 s from the floor cells, 0.3, 2.1 and 5.1 s from the ceiling cells (11.7, 10.9, 8.0, 2.1, 2.1, 8.0, 11.9 s on the old law, which `--recovery-law lookahead` still flies and every bundle from before that date re-flies on). The gate is the deepest cell's 10 m at the cap, 5.0 s, plus two ticks: still implementation-derived, now from the cap, not from the forecast. Still open from the 30 m cell: ArduPilot's RTL entered above RTL_ALT (15 m) returns at its current altitude, so an RTL from above the 20 m ceiling would reach home still above it; whether a ceiling breach should make RTL descend first is a design question the grant does not answer. Since 2026-10-12 guardrail/rtl_path.py reports such a leg as blocked (its return altitude is outside the band), so an RTL from there takes G6 and lands; no cell here reaches RTL, so it is not exercised here.

Was a KNOWN FAILURE from 2026-10-07 to 2026-10-09: a FALSE fail-safe through edge X6. THE ANSWER TO THE 2026-09-02 REVIEW, made measurable.
Prof. Lai's point was fair: BoT-SORT and ByteTrack associate detections across frames better than we do, so "we track well" is not a claim worth making. But a tracker must be given a BOX and cannot be given a NOUN. It returns an ID; it never returns a CLASS.
The stand-off rule is written per class - 10 m from a pedestrian, 5 m from anything else - so the policy needs to know the subject IS a person before it can pick the rule. That is not a tracking-quality contest the open-vocabulary detector might lose; it is a question a tracker cannot be asked at all.
Here one object never moves and the policy is never edited. Only the class word attached to it changes, twelve seconds in, and the enforced ring goes from 5 m to 10 m. Both rules come from policies/sitl_pedestrian.yaml exactly as it already shipped - nothing was added for this scenario, which is the point: the capability was in the schema the whole time.
WHY ITS LABEL ACCEPTS P0 TICKS UNDER THE AUTOPILOT (2026-11-02): the Loiter timeout's RTL (rubric E5) flies straight home past the pedestrian, its forecast inside the 10 m ring on 4 RTL ticks, and the aircraft passes inside the ring once (an autopilot breach): the modelled RTL, like ArduPilot's, knows nothing of a stand-off, and guardrail/rtl_path.py judges zones and the band only.

THE OPEN DEFECT, pinned here so it stops living only in a document. The subject sits exactly on the route, so every direction that makes progress also closes the range. The Shield never emits an illegal action - the P0 gate holds - but the mission wedges: the aircraft cannot get past the subject and never reaches its goal. Recorded on 2026-08-31 as the gap between "the action was repaired" and "the trajectory was sensible". When this scenario starts PASSING, the defect is fixed and the marker should come off.

results.why:
standoff-approach from drawn directions, with the declared subject 7, 9 or 12 m off the route as a pedestrian (10 m ring) or a car (5 m ring). At 7 and 9 m the pedestrian ring crosses the route and the Shield has to take the aircraft round it; the car ring never does. Either way the binding ring must hold and the mission must finish.
9 m with a pedestrian was a known failure from 2026-10-07 to 2026-10-12: a false fail-safe through theta and the Loiter timeout (the first StandoffHold moved the forecast 2.1 m, over the 2.0 m lateral theta, so the FSM abandoned projection, X1 then G3; LOITER held, the pilot kept asking, and the 30 s timeout, G5, sent the aircraft home; never unsafe, P0 clean). On the shipped default it now passes in the library and on all three nightly variants and seeds, on either theta reading; with the onset limit at 0 s it fails again (measured 2026-10-11 and 2026-10-12). Its pin was removed on 2026-10-12. The onset limit is the PI's question 11 and theta's reading question 1 (docs/DESIGN-escalation-fsm.md, Questions for the PI): if the PI's answers bring the failure back, so does the pin.
results.known_failure_reason: False fail-safe through theta and the Loiter timeout (re-measured 2026-11-02; until 2026-10-12 it came through N-in-T flicker): the pedestrian's 10 m ring crosses the route, and the first forecast that meets it reaches more than theta into it, so the FSM abandons projection on tick 0 (X1, then G3: Loiter). The autopilot holds the aircraft where the deep request stays deep, and the operator's 30 s timeout (G5) sends it home. Flown without a fail-safe, the projection takes the aircraft round the ring and its requests are over theta for 1.5 s only (rubric N1): the escalation, not the pilot, made the unsafe request persist. Never unsafe, P0 clean. The decided theta basis (each repair's forecast depth) is what fires; docs/RUBRIC-failsafe.md section 5.

The onset limit is the PI's question 11 and theta's reading question 1 (docs/DESIGN-escalation-fsm.md, Questions for the PI): if the PI's answers bring the failure back, so does the pin.

The grant's worked example, as far as the Shield can take it: a polygon no-fly zone hot-applied mid-flight (Shield.hot_apply, generation 0 -> 1), its near edge `ahead_m` in front of the aircraft on its current heading. 3 m ahead leaves 2 m to the margin ring, so the reaction has to be immediate. At the grant's 5 s forecast (2026-10-12) every spawn but 30 m is inside the lookahead at 4 m/s (20 m), and 30 m is inside it at 8 m/s (40 m); at the 3 s forecast flown until then only 3 m (and 6 m at 4 m/s) were. The purpose holds: a zone appearing inside the forecast must be answered on the spawn tick. The zone never moves (dyn-nfz-translate below is the moving version), so the goal behind it is not reached, and no outcome is labelled.

The zone appears centred ON the aircraft (the reference repository's test_dynamic_nfz_spawn_on_top, flown): legal one tick, inside a P0 zone the next through no action of its own. It must get out, and must not fly back in. The time bound is the Shield's own numbers: half the 40 m zone plus the 1 m margin at GeofenceEscape's 2 m/s is 10.5 s. size_m=20 variant 0 was a known failure from 2026-10-07 to 2026-10-09: from that approach angle GeofenceEscape takes more than T = 5 s to get out, and X6, which tested duration only, sent the aircraft to RTL while the escape was still converging. Since X6's progress test (2026-10-09) the escape is left alone (G1 then G7) and is out in 5.6 s; re-measured 2026-10-11 on both theta readings and both onset limits, and the marker was removed then.

A 40 x 4 m bar spawned beside the route at 3 s (its centre 15 m to the right, lying along the track), rotated 90 degrees about its centre at 8 s (rotate_polygon_fence, a step): it now lies across the track and blocks the route ahead of the aircraft. Before the rotation nothing may bind; after it the aircraft must be held out of the bar.

The same bar, spinning: spawned across the route 25 m ahead of the aircraft at 3 s and turning about its centre at `deg_per_s` (rotate_polygon_fence with a yaw rate), so it opens and closes the route. The Shield forecasts the rotation; the aircraft must never fly itself into the bar. Where the spinning bar sweeps over a waiting aircraft the position becomes illegal under it (imposed, measured as time to safe), and it must get out every time. At the grant's 5 s forecast (2026-10-12) the bar never reaches the waiting aircraft: the Shield forecasts 15-30 degrees of rotation instead of 9-18, its first brake comes 2 s earlier (3.4 s against 5.4 s), and the aircraft waits clear of the sweep (closest 1.04 m at 3 deg/s and 1.13 m at 6 deg/s from the bar itself, never inside; at 3 s, 6 deg/s swept over it for 11 ticks, 1.84 m deep). Bars of 50 and 56 m (measured the same day) do not change that. The 6 deg/s pin (below until 2026-10-12) came off: at 5 s the cell takes G1, G2, then G8 (Loiter cleared) and G7, and completes. So that the imposed half is still flown here (the review of 2026-10-12: with 3 and 6 deg/s alone the time-to-safe gate passed on nothing), 9 deg/s was added: there the sweep does come over the waiting aircraft (inside the bar's ring at 8.3 s, 0.94 m from the bar; time to safe 5.1 s, never censored), and it flew the old 6 deg/s chain - pinned until 2026-10-19 (below). Since then the FSM's hold point is judged against the sweep (guardrail/holdpoint.py): at 8.3 s the in-place LOITER the bar is about to cover is replaced by a point 1.0 m away, at (-183.9, -4.5), legal from arrival through the lookahead (0.25 s away), the bar passes, the Loiter clears (G8), and a second N-in-T Loiter later also clears: G1 G2 G8 G1 G2 G8, no fail-safe, 0 P0 ticks flown (50 before), all three nightly seeds. 12 deg/s and faster were measured and not added: at 12 the harness counts one breach (a move of the aircraft's own onto a spot the sweep had already made unsafe), at 18 and 24 the forecast exceeds theta (X1) and the Loiter timeout (G5) sends it home.

The curfew fence (weekdays 07:30-17:30) goes out of force while the aircraft is held at its edge: the scenario clock starts at 17:29:40 or 17:29:50 and advances with simulated time, so the window closes at 17:30:00, 20 s or 10 s in. results.why:
corridor-drift-out's pilot (aimed straight out of the side at `ask_mps`) with the corridor narrowed mid-flight: at 3 s the 40 m route is swapped for one 10 m wide on the same centreline. Before the swap the old half-width (20 m) binds; after it the aircraft must be brought back inside 5 m and held there against a pilot still pulling out.
WHY ITS LABEL ACCEPTS P0 TICKS UNDER THE AUTOPILOT (2026-11-02): the Loiter timeout's RTL (rubric E5) flies the straight leg home, its forecast crossing the narrowed corridor's wall on 4-8 RTL ticks; it ends inside the corridor.

Before the swap the old half-width (20 m) binds; after it the aircraft must be brought back inside 5 m and held there against a pilot still pulling out.
WHY ITS LABEL ACCEPTS P0 TICKS UNDER THE AUTOPILOT (2026-11-02): the Loiter timeout's RTL (rubric E5) flies the straight leg home, its forecast crossing the narrowed corridor's wall on 4-8 RTL ticks; it ends inside the corridor.

A zone whose breach action is RTL is hot-applied `ahead_m` in front of the aircraft at 3 s. The Shield does not project around it: the rule asks for RTL, so it stops where a stop is legal and the escalation FSM goes straight to RTL (edge G11). The autopilot's RTL flies home, behind the aircraft, away from the zone. Labelled RTL_triggered with a fail-safe expected; the aircraft must never enter the zone.

A zone whose breach action is RTL is hot-applied `ahead_m` in front of the aircraft at 3 s. The Shield does not project around it: the rule asks for RTL, so it stops where a stop is legal and the escalation FSM goes straight to RTL (edge G11). The autopilot's RTL flies home, behind the aircraft, away from the zone. Labelled RTL_triggered with a fail-safe expected; the aircraft must never enter the zone.

The same, with breach action `land`: the FSM goes straight to Land (G12) and the autopilot descends at 0.5 m/s until it is down (G10, the episode ends). The descent takes the aircraft below the demo policy's 10 m floor: those ticks are the AUTOPILOT's, left out of the Shield's own escape count and counted in `true_p0_flown_ticks` (the true-state record), so a reader sees the floor broken by the landing rather than a clean figure. Labelled Land_triggered with a fail-safe expected. WHY ITS LABEL ACCEPTS P0 TICKS UNDER THE AUTOPILOT: a landing ends below any altitude floor by definition, so every LAND tick whose forecast crosses the 10 m floor is a P0 tick the autopilot flew (`autopilot_p0_flown_ticks_by_mode` LAND, 249 of 300 at the grant's 5 s forecast; 229 at 3 s, where the forecast saw the floor later). The rule asked for the landing; the floor cannot hold under it.

Breach action `loiter`: the FSM goes to Loiter directly (X4) and the autopilot holds position, while the pilot keeps asking to fly into the zone, so the hard rule is never clear for T_recover. After the operator-defined Loiter timeout (30 s, fsm.FSMConfig) the FSM sends the aircraft home (G5). Labelled RTL_triggered with a fail-safe expected: the fail-safe here is reached through the timeout, not a direct action.

The way home is blocked. At 4 s a zone is hot-applied BEHIND the aircraft, across the line between it and the launch point; at 5 s a zone whose breach action is RTL appears 12 m ahead, so the FSM goes straight to RTL (G11). ArduPilot's RTL would fly the straight leg home at 15 m through the first zone. guardrail/rtl_path.py tests that leg against every P0 zone in force on the first RTL tick, reports it blocked, and the FSM takes the grant's RTL -> Land edge (G6, "RTL fails (battery / blocked path)"), then lands where it is (G10). Labelled Land_triggered with a fail-safe expected; the autopilot must never enter either zone. WHY ITS LABEL ACCEPTS P0 TICKS UNDER THE AUTOPILOT: the landing goes through the demo policy's 10 m floor, as in failsafe-land-zone, so the LAND ticks whose forecast crosses it are P0 ticks the autopilot flew. Whether the FSM should hold instead of landing when the way home is blocked is the FSM's question (it lands, as the grant's diagram draws it).

reasons: blocked path: the leg home at 15 m crosses home-side-zone (8.0 m inside its ring)

results.why: The battery goes critical during the RTL. A zone whose breach action is RTL appears 12 m ahead at 10 s; the FSM goes to RTL (G11) and the autopilot flies home, 40 m behind. At 14 s, halfway home, the battery reports critical (stress.battery_critical_at_s, the battery hook of guardrail/rtl_path.py): the RTL in progress fails and the FSM takes the grant's RTL -> Land edge (G6), then lands where it is (G10). With no critical battery the same flight reaches home (G9). Labelled Land_triggered with a fail-safe expected; never inside either zone. WHY ITS LABEL ACCEPTS P0 TICKS UNDER THE AUTOPILOT: the LAND descent goes through the demo policy's 10 m floor (see failsafe-land-zone), so its ticks whose forecast crosses the floor are P0 ticks the autopilot flew.

The matrix row's "high-speed", which the 4 m/s demo policy cannot fly: policies/wgs84_taipei.yaml caps at 12 m/s, so a pilot asking 8, 12 or 20 m/s really flies 8-12 m/s - 1.2 m per 0.1 s tick - past the school-yard zone's north face (y 40.3) on a line 0.2, 0.5 or 0.8 m inside its 1 m margin ring, or exactly on it (41.3). No scenario clock, so the zone's weekday curfew is in force (absent clock = every rule active). It must never enter the ring, never exceed 12 m/s, and still get past. One face only: the zone is not square (78 x 80.6 m), so a rotation would move the line relative to the face it meets.
40.8 m at 12 m/s was a known failure from 2026-10-07 to 2026-10-12 (the edge flicker below). Since the FSM counts at most one onset per second (onset limit, 2026-10-09) it passes on the shipped default, in the library and on all three nightly seeds, and on either theta reading; with the onset limit at 0 s it fails again (measured 2026-10-11 and 2026-10-12). Its pin was removed on 2026-10-12. The limit is the PI's question 11 (docs/DESIGN-escalation-fsm.md, Questions for the PI): if the PI picks 0 s, the pin comes back.
RE-PINNED 2026-10-12 at the grant's 5 s forecast (the cells are deterministic, so one run measures every seed). The flicker moved: 40.5 m at 12 m/s, 40.8 m at 8 m/s and 41.1 m at 8 m/s now pass (G1>G7>G1>G7, the goal reached), and 40.5 m at 8 m/s (G1>G7>G1>G2>G5) and 40.8 m at 12 m/s (G1>G2>G5>G9) now fail by the same mechanism. Which cells flicker depends on where along the face the forecast's poses land on the ring, so it moves with the forecast; the pins follow the measurement.

tests/test_guardrail_coverage.py's unit case, flown: below the 10 m floor, asking 8-11 m/s against a 4 m/s cap, descending at 3 m/s, and pointed at the no-fly zone 4 m away - from a drawn approach angle. Repair operators have to interact without oscillating (bounded iteration); the aircraft must climb out exactly once and never enter the zone. KNOWN FAILURE IN EVERY CELL since the escalation FSM was wired into the Shield (2026-10-07): a FALSE fail-safe. The first repair's AltitudeFix is 12-18 m at the grant's 5 s forecast (8-14 m at 3 s) against the grant's 0.5 m vertical theta, so the FSM abandons projection at once (X1 then G3: Brake -> Loiter). Until 2026-10-19 ArduPilot's LOITER held the aircraft where it was, below the floor (48 P0 ticks of LOITER), and five seconds of an illegal position later X6 sent it home (X1 G3 X6 G9, 9.6 s). Since then the FSM's hold point is chosen legally (guardrail/holdpoint.py): a stop below the floor is illegal at every horizontal position, so the hold is moved straight up to 10.5 m, 0.5 m inside the band, the modelled autopilot climbs there at 2 m/s, and X6 no longer fires (the illegal depth falls at the climb rate). That part is robust. The labels are not: the pilot keeps asking for the illegal action, so the Loiter never clears (G8), and 30 s after G3 the operator-defined Loiter timeout (G5, ours) sends the aircraft home: X1 G3 G5 G9, RTL at 30.1 s, home at 31.9 s, the zone never entered, the episode ends safe and P0 clean - a fail-safe the label does not expect. At the library's default 300 ticks the run ended in Loiter 0.2 s before G5 and the cell read as a pass (2026-10-19); this family now flies 400 ticks so that pass cannot come back by accident. Whether a pilot that asks for an illegal action for 30 s SHOULD be sent home - the label, or our 30 s timeout - is a question for the PI (docs/DESIGN-hold-points.md). ANSWERED 2026-11-02 by the fail-safe rubric the PI delegated (docs/RUBRIC-failsafe.md): it should. Flown without a fail-safe, the pilot's requests are repairs over theta for the whole run (clause E5: an unsafe repair that persists past the operator timeout), so the timeout's RTL is the fail-safe the grant asks for ("trigger fail-safe (RTL / Land) when repair is unsafe", p1) and the labels are now RTL_triggered, fail-safe expected; the known-failure marker came off. The variant-2 forecast-tunnelling record (2026-10-06) is kept below as a comment.
WHY ITS LABEL ACCEPTS P0 TICKS UNDER THE AUTOPILOT: the moved hold's climb into the band flies 1 LOITER tick whose forecast is still under the 10 m floor, and the Loiter timeout's RTL (the fail-safe the rubric expects, E5, since 2026-11-02) flies 18 RTL ticks whose forecast crosses the 20 m ceiling while it climbs to the return altitude; the zone is never entered.

Stability under sensor degradation, inside the error budget the 1 m margin was sized for: white position noise of 0.2-0.3 m (3 sigma under 0.9 m) and up to 2 ticks of state latency (0.8 m stale at 4 m/s). The target line runs INSIDE the margin ring (0.4-0.8 m from the zone), so the aircraft slides along the ring pressing in - the configuration where noise matters. A line parallel to the edge outside the ring was measured insensitive to 2 m noise, and a line inside the zone itself meets its face head-on and wedges, so neither tests anything here. The polygon itself must never be entered. The Shield's own escape count is the grant's; true-state violations are reported beside it.
Pins re-measured 2026-10-12 on the shipped default. Since the FSM counts at most one onset per second (onset limit, 2026-10-09) these cells pass on every seed measured (library 0, nightly 1001-1003) and their known-failure pins were removed: latency 0 / pass_y 23.2 / sigma 0.2 (every seed); latency 0 / 23.6 / 0.2 (seed 0); latency 1 / 23.2 / 0.2 (1002); latency 2 / 23.2 / 0.3 (1003); latency 2 / 23.6 / 0.3 (1002). Three pins that named every seed now name only the seeds where the cell still fails: latency 0 / 23.2 / 0.3 passes on seeds 0 and 1003, latency 0 / 23.6 / 0.3 on 0, 1001 and 1003, and latency 1 / 23.2 / 0.3 on 1001-1003. With the onset limit at 0 s (every return counts) every one of those cells fails again, on every seed measured (2026-10-12, the library and the nightly profile). The limit is the PI's question 11 (docs/DESIGN-escalation-fsm.md, Questions for the PI): if the PI picks 0 s, the pins come back. At the grant's 5 s forecast (later on 2026-10-12) the seeds that flicker moved again: only latency 0 / 23.2 / 0.3 fails, on 1001 and 1003; the comment above known_failures lists what came off.

A line parallel to the edge outside the ring was measured insensitive to 2 m noise, and a line inside the zone itself meets its face head-on and wedges, so neither tests anything here. The polygon itself must never be entered. The Shield's own escape count is the grant's; true-state violations are reported beside it.
Pins re-measured 2026-10-12 on the shipped default. Since the FSM counts at most one onset per second (onset limit, 2026-10-09) these cells pass on every seed measured (library 0, nightly 1001-1003) and their known-failure pins were removed: latency 0 / pass_y 23.2 / sigma 0.2 (every seed); latency 0 / 23.6 / 0.2 (seed 0); latency 1 / 23.2 / 0.2 (1002); latency 2 / 23.2 / 0.3 (1003); latency 2 / 23.6 / 0.3 (1002). Three pins that named every seed now name only the seeds where the cell still fails: latency 0 / 23.2 / 0.3 passes on seeds 0 and 1003, latency 0 / 23.6 / 0.3 on 0, 1001 and 1003, and latency 1 / 23.2 / 0.3 on 1001-1003. With the onset limit at 0 s (every return counts) every one of those cells fails again, on every seed measured (2026-10-12, the library and the nightly profile). The limit is the PI's question 11 (docs/DESIGN-escalation-fsm.md, Questions for the PI): if the PI picks 0 s, the pins come back. At the grant's 5 s forecast (later on 2026-10-12) the seeds that flicker moved again: only latency 0 / 23.2 / 0.3 fails, on 1001 and 1003; the comment above known_failures lists what came off.

Beyond the budget, TRACKED rather than gated: 1-2 m noise and 5-10 ticks (0.5-1 s) of latency against a 1 m margin. Gated only on what must hold whatever the sensor does: the Shield never emits an action it has itself found illegal, and never a non-finite one.

TRACKED: GPS denial as a headless run can model it. For the window the Shield is handed the LAST FIX, frozen, while the aircraft keeps flying - what a bridge that forwards the last pose would do. The Shield's State has no fix-quality field, so it cannot know the pose is stale, and the grant names no Shield response to GPS loss. Measured 2026-10-06 on the head-on lane, at the 3 s forecast flown then: frozen while parked at the lookahead edge (6-11 s), the Shield keeps permitting the ~3.9 m/s it would allow from 11.6 m out and the aircraft ends 7 m inside the polygon; a 2-4 s window at 2 s never reaches it. RE-CUT 2026-10-12 for the grant's 5 s forecast. The long windows were 5 s, the old lookahead plus 2 s, starting at 2, 4 and 6 s; at 5 s the Shield brakes the head-on lane 20.6 m out by 5 s, so a dropout from 6 s froze a pose it was already holding and changed nothing (no entry). The long windows are now the new lookahead plus 2 s (7 s), from 2, 4 and 6 s: frozen at 4 s, still at 4 m/s about 24 m out, the Shield keeps permitting 4 m/s for 7 s and the aircraft ends 7 m inside the polygon (4-11 s, the cell the finding is pinned on); from 2 s it stops on the ring (1.0 m from the polygon), and from 6 s it is already held and nothing changes (20.6 m). The 2-4 s window still never reaches it. On the edge lane (23.6) no window enters. Gated only on what must hold whatever the sensor does - the Shield never emits an action it has itself found illegal, never a non-finite one - and on the dropout having actually frozen the pose (a window that froze nothing would otherwise pass as a clean run). Unlabelled until 2026-11-02 ("with no fix-status input there is no defensible fail-safe expectation to write down"). The rubric (docs/RUBRIC-failsafe.md) reads the expectation from the ground truth, not from what the Shield can see: a frozen fix held while the aircraft moves farther than the margin, within that error of a P0 boundary, expects a fail-safe (E3). The Shield has no fix-quality input, so where the FSM does not trigger for another reason it is a missed trigger, reported as such (lane 23.6 with the 2-9 s and 6-13 s windows).
WHY ITS LABEL ACCEPTS P0 TICKS UNDER THE AUTOPILOT (2026-11-02): on lane 23.6 with the 4-11 s window the Loiter timeout's RTL (the fix was frozen beyond the margin, rubric E3) is blocked and the FSM lands (G6): 1 RTL tick, then 33 LAND ticks through the 10 m floor and one autopilot breach of it - a landing ends below any floor.

Measured 2026-10-06 on the head-on lane, at the 3 s forecast flown then: frozen while parked at the lookahead edge (6-11 s), the Shield keeps permitting the ~3.9 m/s it would allow from 11.6 m out and the aircraft ends 7 m inside the polygon; a 2-4 s window at 2 s never reaches it. RE-CUT 2026-10-12 for the grant's 5 s forecast. The long windows were 5 s, the old lookahead plus 2 s, starting at 2, 4 and 6 s; at 5 s the Shield brakes the head-on lane 20.6 m out by 5 s, so a dropout from 6 s froze a pose it was already holding and changed nothing (no entry). The long windows are now the new lookahead plus 2 s (7 s), from 2, 4 and 6 s: frozen at 4 s, still at 4 m/s about 24 m out, the Shield keeps permitting 4 m/s for 7 s and the aircraft ends 7 m inside the polygon (4-11 s, the cell the finding is pinned on); from 2 s it stops on the ring (1.0 m from the polygon), and from 6 s it is already held and nothing changes (20.6 m). The 2-4 s window still never reaches it. On the edge lane (23.6) no window enters. Gated only on what must hold whatever the sensor does - the Shield never emits an action it has itself found illegal, never a non-finite one - and on the dropout having actually frozen the pose (a window that froze nothing would otherwise pass as a clean run). Unlabelled until 2026-11-02 ("with no fix-status input there is no defensible fail-safe expectation to write down"). The rubric (docs/RUBRIC-failsafe.md) reads the expectation from the ground truth, not from what the Shield can see: a frozen fix held while the aircraft moves farther than the margin, within that error of a P0 boundary, expects a fail-safe (E3). The Shield has no fix-quality input, so where the FSM does not trigger for another reason it is a missed trigger, reported as such (lane 23.6 with the 2-9 s and 6-13 s windows).
WHY ITS LABEL ACCEPTS P0 TICKS UNDER THE AUTOPILOT (2026-11-02): on lane 23.6 with the 4-11 s window the Loiter timeout's RTL (the fix was frozen beyond the margin, rubric E3) is blocked and the FSM lands (G6): 1 RTL tick, then 33 LAND ticks through the 10 m floor and one autopilot breach of it - a landing ends below any floor.

A steady wind the Shield cannot see (it predicts with the commanded action only), within what ArduCopter's position controller can hold against, blowing along the route into the zone (0 deg in the mission's frame, the tailwind that defeated the margin on the open-loop model), on the head-on lane (y 15) and the edge lane (y 25, 1 m outside the margin). The polygon itself must never be entered and the aircraft must always get back out of the margin.
RE-CUT 2026-10-12 for the closed-loop wind model. GUIDED velocity setpoints run AC_PosControl's position loop (the velocity target is integrated into a position target, PSC_POSXY_P 1.0, and the velocity PID has an integrator), so a Brake's zero setpoint holds its position and a wind below the hold authority changes nothing: every cell flies its lane's calm flight. Measured that day, at the grant's 5 s forecast, with the open-loop model the harness flew until then, seven cells of the 1-3 m/s sweep ended in a false fail-safe (five at the 3 s forecast): the tailwind into the zone on the head-on lane (0 deg, every speed: parked at the ring with a zero setpoint and blown in, the repair over theta, LOITER, the 30 s timeout, RTL), the 1 m/s headwind on that lane, and the edge lane with the wind toward the zone at 1, 2 and 3 m/s (N-in-T flicker at the ring, then the timeout). The 0 deg pin (since 2026-10-06) and the 1 and 3 m/s edge-lane pins (since 2026-10-07) came off on 2026-10-12: under the closed loop each cell passes, and the open-loop model still reproduces the false trigger (tests/test_harnesstruth_wind.py). Within the hold authority neither speed nor direction changes the flight any more, so the sweep is one wind per lane: 5 m/s (the strongest of the grant example's values) as a tailwind (0 deg), the direction that failed on the head-on lane. Two cells: each lane's labelled null that shows the wind rejected. It was 24 cells (1-3 m/s x four directions) until 2026-10-12 and 8 (2 and 5 m/s x 0 and 270 deg) in that day's first re-cut, which the review of the same day found to be two flights flown four times each - 6 copies counted in the headline fail-safe score and its never-trigger null. What this cannot see: the velocity loop's transients as drag changes with the commanded velocity, which the kinematic harness leaves out with or without wind, and an airspeed limit upwind (experiments/sweep_scenarios.py, "optimistic upwind").

TRACKED: a tailwind into the zone beyond the hold authority, on the head-on lane (y 15, through the zone's centre) and an off-centre lane (y 20, 3 m inside the zone's face). 8 m/s is beyond the modelled authority (6.4 m/s, the lower end of the SITL default frame at the 30 deg ANGLE_MAX) and 12 m/s beyond its upper end (11.5 m/s) too, so 12 m/s is beyond the airframe's authority whatever its drag split. No setpoint the Shield or the autopilot can fly holds the aircraft out: the excess wind carries it in, and a fail-safe is expected (the label). Tracked, not gated on the polygon, because beyond authority the polygon cannot hold by construction; gated on the Shield's own escape count and finite actions (a landing ends below the floor, so "got out" is not a gate here either). What each cell flew is measured in the published sweep and summarised in the CHANGELOG entry of 2026-10-12. WHY ITS LABEL ACCEPTS P0 TICKS UNDER THE AUTOPILOT: beyond authority the LOITER hold, the RTL leg and the LAND descent are all carried by the wind (into the zone, or through the 10 m floor for LAND); the autopilot cannot fly a legal action, and those ticks are counted per mode rather than hidden. A hold that drifts straight through the zone can clear the hard rule on the far side before any Loiter -> RTL edge fires (N-in-T, the 30 s timeout, X6 and X7 all need seconds): a missed fail-safe by the label, and a question for the FSM (an FSM that knew its hold was not holding would escalate), not for this harness. Answered on 2026-11-02: in Loiter X6 / X7 judge the aircraft's own position (guardrail/fsm.py loiter_x67 "position") instead of waiting for the unflown request to violate a hard rule, and G8 needs the position legal; lane 15 at 12 m/s now goes G1 G3 X7 (7.4 s, the hold losing ground) G6 (no progress home into the wind) and lands off the zone, where it went G1 G3 G8 and was handed back on the far side at 8.9 s. The landing descends through the 10 m floor: 106 more autopilot LAND ticks at the true state than the missed fail-safe flew. Until 2026-10-12 this cell flew 5 m/s on the open-loop model, where the Shield's setpoints drifted with the wind and the modelled autopilot rejected it entirely; on the closed loop 5 m/s is within authority and is wind-within-authority's.

results.why: TRACKED: 2 m/s wind from a direction drawn from the seed, plus 0.5 m/s gusts and a start jittered up to 1 m, so each seed is a different flight - the family that makes the nightly profile's three seeds mean something. Gated only on the Shield's own escape count and finite actions; where the gusts carry the aircraft is reported, not gated, because a drawn direction cannot carry a fixed expectation. Since 2026-10-12 the steady wind is rejected and a gust is pulled back to the position target at PSC_POSXY_P (an offset of about 0.12 m, sigma), so the seeds still differ, by centimetres; 3 m/s flew the same flights as 2 m/s and was dropped. On the open-loop model a gust random-walked the aircraft and the steady wind carried it; one cell (lane 25, 2 m/s, seed 0) was blown into a LOITER hold whose forecast crossed the ring, 50 P0 ticks flown by the autopilot (published 2026-10-12, before the change), and on library seed 0 all four cells of the 2-3 m/s sweep ended in a fail-safe their label does not expect (at 3 s and at 5 s); on the closed loop none does.
